projectsPage.subtitle: Student projects in AI, hardware and applications.

flapeeg.title: FlapEEG
flapeeg.description: An innovative video game controlled by brain waves (EEG). Discover how AI and neurotechnology let you pilot a virtual bird with your thoughts. A pioneer brain–computer interface project open to every profile (neuro, AI, dev, design).
flapeeg.homeDescription: Play FlapEEG with your brainwaves: AI reads EEG signals to control the bird.
flapeeg.nominationBadge: Nominated at Gala de la vie étudiante 2025

f1tenth.title: F1Tenth
f1tenth.description: In partnership with the VAUL student club (owner of the F1TENTH car), develop a control mode via EMG bracelet. Objective: detect arm movements from muscle signals, interpret them with AI, then convert them into driving commands (steering/speed) to control the vehicle. Project focused on EMG and AI.
f1tenth.homeDescription: Control a 1/10 F1TENTH car with an EMG bracelet: AI turns arm movement into steering and speed.

decisiontree.title: TreeCore
decisiontree.description: Research and development around decision trees: explore classic and advanced algorithms, optimize automated decision-making, and help deliver open-source tooling for AI. Ideal for students in data science, mathematics, and computer science.

lenia.title: Lenia
lenia.description: Autonomous cellular automata inspired by artificial life: simulate virtual creatures capable of emergence, evolution, and interaction. This project combines mathematics, simulation, AI, and scientific visualization. Join us to explore digital life and creative algorithms.

mangaai.title: MangaAI
mangaai.description: Automatic manga translation and analysis powered by AI: OCR, NLP, dialogue generation, and style analysis. Help build tools for Japanese culture, computational linguistics, and computer vision. Perfect for fans of AI, manga, and language processing.
mangaai.homeDescription: Translate manga panels with AI using OCR, language processing, and context-aware text replacement.

canlock.title: CANlock
canlock.description: Partner project with Thales: design an intelligent system to detect attacks on the vehicle CAN bus. Objective: reduce false positives and deliver a production-ready pipeline. Profiles sought: AI/Data, Cybersecurity, Embedded.

drone.title: Drone - Laser Tag
drone.homeDescription: Design and build an autonomous FPV drone to compete in a laser tag competition.
drone.description: Build a turnkey laser system for an autonomous FPV competition: 180° sensor, emission module, custom PCB, and centralized management software. Academic partner: Philippe Giguère. Team Lead: Anthony Lavertu.

sgd-beyond.title: SGD - Beyond
sgd-beyond.description: Analyze and enhance a foundational AI algorithm (SGD) by integrating a noise-based optimization method. Find more details and code on GitHub.

nutrinov.title: NutriNov
nutrinov.description: Identify a real nutritional challenge and develop a viable tech prototype — in partnership with Open Food Facts. Project type: Entrepreneurial initiative. Team Lead: Eloïse Prevot.

poppy-conception.title: Poppy Humanoid (Conception)
poppy-conception.description: 3D print components, assemble joints, and integrate electronics for an open-source humanoid robot. Join the project to contribute to mechanical and mechatronic design.

poppy-simulation.title: Poppy Humanoid (Simulation)
poppy-simulation.description: Teach a robot to walk by developing reinforcement learning algorithms in simulation and transferring them to the real robot. Join the project to explore robotic AI.

asldecoder.title: ASL Decoder
asldecoder.description: Raspberry Pi system with camera for real-time American Sign Language (ASL) recognition using AI. Completed project combining computer vision and machine learning.

avion-cargo.title: Avion-Cargo
avion-cargo.description: Autonomous precision landing system using computer vision. ArUco marker detection, real-time 3D estimation and intelligent guidance for sub-10 cm landings.

privacyPage.title: Privacy policy
privacyPage.intro: A plain-language account of what this website handles, why it is used, who may receive it and the choices available to you.

atGlance.title: At a glance
atGlance.contact: The partnership form stays in your browser and only opens a draft in your email app.
atGlance.analytics: Optional Vercel audience and performance measurements remain off until you allow them.
atGlance.noSale: We do not sell personal information or use advertising pixels.

responsible.title: Who is responsible
responsible.body: The Club Intelligence Artificielle – Université Laval (CIA ULaval) operates this website. The person responsible for the protection of personal information at CIA ULaval is the designated contact for questions, requests and complaints about personal information.

information.title: Information we handle and how we receive it

messages.title: Messages you choose to send
messages.body: The partnership form does not submit information to this website or a database. It prepares an email draft on your device. If you send that draft, the Club receives the required name and reply address, any optional organization and message you entered, and the usual email metadata. Nothing reaches the Club until you send the email.

technical.title: Site delivery and optional measurements
technical.body: Like any hosted website, Vercel may process request data needed to deliver and secure the site, such as an IP address, request time, route and browser information. Only after you allow analytics, Vercel Web Analytics may process the route, referrer, filtered query parameters, browser, operating system, device, approximate location down to city and a request hash that rotates every 24 hours. Speed Insights measures route-level Web Vitals and related device, browser, network, country and timing information. Vercel describes these measurement results as anonymous or aggregated. We do not send custom analytics events.

storage.title: Preferences stored on your device
storage.body: The site stores your selected language under “i18nextLng” and your analytics choice under “cia.analyticsConsent.v1” in browser local storage. These strictly functional values remember your choices; they are not used for advertising. Clearing this site’s browser data removes them.

purposes.title: Why we use information
purposes.body: We use correspondence to answer you, discuss membership or partnerships, keep necessary administrative records and protect the Club. We use technical request data to deliver and secure the site. If you opt in, we use audience and performance measurements only to understand use of the site and improve its content, loading and responsiveness.

sharing.title: Who may receive information
sharing.body: Messages are handled by your email provider, our institutional email service and the Club officers who need them to answer or manage the relationship. Website administrators and Vercel may access technical data only as needed to provide, secure and maintain the service. Google Fonts receives a technical request from your browser to deliver the site’s typefaces; Google states that its Fonts API does not set cookies. Links to Discord, social media, GitHub and other websites are governed by those services’ own privacy practices. We do not sell or rent personal information.

transfers.title: Processing outside Québec
transfers.body: Vercel, Google and email service providers may process technical or message data outside Québec and Canada where they or their subprocessors operate. Their safeguards, service agreements and the laws of those jurisdictions may apply.

retention.title: Retention and safeguards
retention.body: We keep correspondence only as long as reasonably needed to answer, manage the relationship, meet administrative or legal requirements and resolve disputes, then delete or anonymize it where appropriate. Vercel measurement retention depends on the service plan and is described in its current documentation. Access is limited to people who need the information, and reasonable safeguards are used. No internet or email transmission can be guaranteed completely secure.

consent.title: Cookies and analytics choices
consent.body: This site does not set advertising or analytics cookies. Because audience measurement can distinguish visits and include approximate location, both Vercel measurement tools are off by default. You can allow or decline them without losing site functionality and change your choice at any time through “Analytics choices” in the footer. If we add non-essential cookies or similar technology, we will update this policy and request consent where required.

rights.title: Your choices and rights
rights.body: You may make a written request to access or correct personal information we hold about you, withdraw consent where applicable, request applicable computerized information in a portable format, or ask how a message was handled. We may verify your identity before responding. You may also complain to the Club’s Privacy Officer and, if needed, Québec’s Commission d’accès à l’information.

contact.title: Contact the person responsible for privacy
contact.body: For a privacy request, question or complaint, contact the person responsible for the protection of personal information at CIA ULaval. Please describe your request clearly; do not email sensitive information unless it is necessary.
contact.subject: Privacy request – CIA ULaval

image.alt: FlappyBrain game interface driven by an EEG headset

description.paragraph1: FlapEEG is a video game that is controlled by thought. We have trained an AI model to interpret brain signals and translate them into actions in the game. For this to work, we equipped ourselves with the latest EEG (electroencephalogram) technology,
description.paragraph2: The format of the game is simple; ever heard of flappy bird? Well, it's the same simple yet fun concept. The only difference is that you control the bird with your thoughts. The simple will to make the little character avoid obstacles is enough to make it move. We are very proud of the work we have accomplished; it may only be the beginning of a video game revolution! Think about it, what if we combined this mechanic to a VR headset? Or, what if this is the skipping stone to helping people with disabilities by giving them power from their own thoughts? The possibilities are endless.

prototype.title: First Prototype
prototype.description: In the video above, you can see the first prototype of the game. Dereck and Louis-Étienne managed to get a simple version of the game up and running where the player could control the character by blinking with an activation threshold.

beginning.description: FlapEEG is a project that started in January 2025. The team consists of 8 members, some of whom are experienced in AI and EEG technology, while others are passionate about video games and coding. They all have different backgrounds and skills, but share the same goal.

dataCollection.title: Collecting Data (Week 2 - Week 4)
dataCollection.subtitle: Data Collection
dataCollection.paragraph1: After successfully establishing the baseline, Jordan recruited volunteers to collect brain data. The goal was to gather a dataset of brain signals while the volunteers played the game to train the AI model.
dataCollection.paragraph2: In the meantime, William finished the game and helped deploying the server with the help of Louis-Étienne.

image.alt: Screenshot of the FlapEEG game interface

filtering.title: Filtering & Training
filtering.subtitle: Filtering & Training
filtering.paragraph1: At this point in the project Louis found out our data wasn't properly filtered and there had a lot of noise which made it unusable. Jordan took care of this and found a way to filter out the noise.
filtering.paragraph2: In the meantime, Amen and Estelle were working hard training the AI model behind the scenes and paving the way for the others to understand the challenges of training a model.

challenge.title: First Challenge
challenge.description: At this point in the project, the team faced a significant challenge: the AI model was not performing as well as needed. They opted to start researching and reading papers to understand the challenges of training a model.

hero.imageAlt: F1Tenth miniature race car controlled by AI and muscle signals
hero.description1: Thrill-seeker? This project will capture your interest! F1 Tenth is a team of students passionate about AI who have successfully combined human and machine. Using an electromyographic bracelet, they managed to control a miniature race car with their muscles.
hero.description2: The team had to train an AI model to read muscle electrical signals and translate them into actions. This involved extensive trial and error to adjust the model's sensitivity and accuracy. The bracelet has multiple sensors, each responsible for a different response like accelerating, braking, or turning. The project was very complex because it required controlling multiple dimensions simultaneously.

hero.paragraph1: Have you ever wondered why your AI model sometimes converges to a mediocre solution when it could do so much better? The answer often lies in the optimization algorithm.
hero.paragraph2: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) is the engine behind training virtually all deep learning models. Yet, despite 20 years of use, this algorithm remains imperfect: it gets stuck in local minima and often misses the best solutions.

simple.subtitle: Autonomous precision landing through computer vision
simple.description1: The Avion-Cargo project focuses on developing a fully autonomous precision landing system using computer vision and artificial intelligence.
simple.description2: The objective is to detect ArUco markers with an onboard camera, estimate the 3D position in real time, then guide the aircraft to achieve a landing precision under 10 cm while enabling payload recovery.
simple.pipelineSubtitle: From visual detection to autonomous aircraft guidance.

pipelineSteps.title: Video capture
pipelineSteps.description: An onboard camera monitors the landing zone in real time.

pipelineSteps.title: ArUco detection
pipelineSteps.description: The system detects ArUco markers to locate the target precisely.

pipelineSteps.title: 3D estimation
pipelineSteps.description: The 3D position is continuously estimated to track the aircraft approach.

pipelineSteps.title: Autonomous guidance
pipelineSteps.description: Advanced navigation algorithms automatically adjust the trajectory.

pipelineSteps.title: Landing and recovery
pipelineSteps.description: Landing targets sub-10 cm precision and enables payload recovery.

summaryItems: Develop a fully autonomous precision landing system.
Detect ArUco markers with an onboard camera.
Estimate 3D position in real time, then guide the aircraft.
Perform landing with precision under 10 cm and recover payloads.
